issues.reason: Inter-clause connectives says a non-finite embedded eventuality carries no status atom of its own "unless its own grammar marks one" ("would V" → Future), and the perfect "to have taken" is exactly such a marking, which Status predicates maps to coarse (Past e) — so the sealed take event must carry (Past sk_take_1).

gaps_confirmed: Direct quotation as the complement of a speech verb ("…," Fleischer said): the instruction set covers a finite that-clause complement and says nothing about quoted speech, its verbatim string, or quoted deixis.

A collective evaluative predicate on a definite plural ("the steps … are insufficient"): the categorical section routes copular predicates on definite plurals through the distributive rule and names only size and name as collection properties, giving no test for a predicate that holds of the set as a whole.
new_gaps: A perfect infinitive under a control verb ("claim to have taken"): the "unless its own grammar marks one" exception names only "would V" → Future, leaving the perfect-infinitive → Past mapping to be inferred from the aspect table.

Ordering inside a seal: the past-perfect rule blocks ordering atoms across a seal boundary but does not say whether two sealed events (the claim and the anterior take) may be related by Before within one seal.
repair_summary: Added (Past sk_take_1) inside the sealed Theme term, after (Patient sk_take_1 sk_step_1), so the perfect infinitive's anteriority is recorded; no ordering atom was added and nothing else changed.
notes: The Past sits inside the seal, so nothing about the taking is asserted at top level — only the sealed proposition now carries its own tense, as the seal rule allows.
